regime.paragraph: Cross-asset moves were small relative to recent volatility: US Treasury yields 2Y -5bp to 4.68% and 10Y unch to 5.00%. The US curve saw a twist steepener in 2s10s (+6bp to 32bp). The dollar fell 0.1%, gold rose 0.2%, the S&P 500 rose 0.3% and Brent rose 0.1%. US high-yield spreads tightened 12bp. The standout move was Dutch TTF gas (+4.9%, 2.1x its 20-day volatility).

regions.name: United States
regions.text: Treasuries rallied with the front end leading, 2Y -5bp to 4.68% and 10Y unch to 5.00%: a twist steepener (2s10s +6bp). Markets removed 11bp of Fed tightening over 12 months (now +65bp). The dollar fell 0.1% and the S&P 500 rose 0.3%.

regions.name: United Kingdom
regions.text: Gilts rallied with the long end leading, 2Y unch to 4.94% and 10Y -3bp to 5.32%: a twist flattener (2s10s -3bp). Gilts outperformed Treasuries by 3bp at 10Y. BoE pricing was steady at +118bp over 12 months. Sterling rose 0.2% and the FTSE 100 rose 0.1%.

regions.name: Europe
regions.text: Bunds sold off with the front end leading, 2Y +5bp to 3.10% and 10Y +3bp to 3.38%: a bear flattener (2s10s -3bp). BTP-Bund tightened 1bp to 113bp. ECB pricing was steady at +59bp over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy. The euro rose 0.3% and the Euro Stoxx 50 rose 0.1%.

relationships.statement: The Treasury curve twisted steeper: easier near-term policy but more long-run risk premium.
relationships.lesson: Front end rallied while the long end sold off: easier policy expected but more long-run risk.

relationships.statement: Gilts outperformed Bunds, pointing to UK-specific relief from data, BoE pricing or fiscal news.
relationships.lesson: Cross-market spreads strip out the global rates move, isolating what was local.

relationships.statement: Narrower Treasury–Bund spreads favoured EUR over USD.
relationships.lesson: FX tends to follow relative rates: a wider US–German yield gap raises the carry on USD versus EUR. Front-end (2Y) differentials usually matter more than 10Y.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Bank of Japan, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 1.04%. Markets price a 38% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 3.5 hikes (88bp) over 12 months; terminal 2.27%. The 12-month pricing moved -34bp on the day. Method: Government bill-curve proxy (indicative). Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +88bp is 3.5 moves.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Federal Reserve, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 4.00%. Markets price a 76% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 2.6 hikes (65bp) over 12 months; terminal 4.89%. The 12-month pricing moved -11bp on the day. Method: Refinitiv OIS curve. Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +65bp is 2.6 moves.

interview.question: Why did Gilts outperform Bunds?
interview.answer: 10Y Gilts moved -3bp versus +3bp for Bunds, so the spread moved -5bp to 194bp (89th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.

interview.question: Why did the US 2Y outperform the 10Y?
interview.answer: The US 2Y moved -5bp and the 10Y unch, so 2s10s moved +6bp to 32bp: a twist steepener. Front end rallied while the long end sold off: easier policy expected but more long-run risk. Market pricing for the Fed over 12 months moved -11bp, which is what drives the front end. Key framework: the 2Y is anchored by expected policy over two years; the 10Y adds term premium and long-run growth and inflation expectations.

interview.question: Why did the UK 10Y outperform the 2Y?
interview.answer: The UK 2Y moved unch and the 10Y -3bp, so 2s10s moved -3bp to 38bp: a twist flattener. Front end sold off while the long end rallied: tighter policy expected, weighing on growth. Market pricing for the BoE over 12 months moved +2bp, which is what drives the front end. Key framework: the 2Y is anchored by expected policy over two years; the 10Y adds term premium and long-run growth and inflation expectations.

flashcards.front: How do you convert OIS pricing into the probability of a 25bp move?
flashcards.back: Probability ≈ implied change at the meeting ÷ 25bp. For example, −18bp priced means about a 72% chance of a 25bp cut.
